data.title: Futu Holdings GAAP EPADS of $2.96 beats by $0.07, revenue of $852.7M beats by $13.3M
data.description:
• Futu Holdings press release (FUTU): Q3 GAAP EPADS of $2.96 beats by $0.07.
  • Revenue of $852.7M (+4.5% Y/Y) beats by $13.3M.
  • Total number of funded accounts1 increased 27.9% year-over-year to 4,005,858 as of September 30, 2026.
  • Total number of brokerage accounts2 increased 22.5% year-over-year to 6,868,829 as of September 30, 2026.
  • Total number of users3 increased 13.8% year-over-year to 32.0 million as of September 30, 2026.
  • Total client assets increased 7.6% year-over-year to HK$1.33 trillion as of September 30, 2026.
  • Daily average client assets were HK$1.33 trillion in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 21.1% from the same period in 2025.
  • Total trading volume in the third quarter of 2026 increased by 28.4% year-over-year to HK$5.01 trillion, in which trading volume for U.S. stocks was HK$3.81 trillion, and trading volume for Hong Kong stocks was HK$942.5 billion.
  • Margin financing and securities lending balance increased 17.1% year-over-year to HK$73.8 billion as of September 30, 2026.

data.title: ATRenew beats top-line and bottom-line estimates; gives Q4 outlook
data.description:

data.title: Elon Musk says Tesla will boost production at Shanghai factory, calls himself a China superfan
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) CEO Elon Musk said the electric vehicle maker would continue increasing production in China, according to Chinese media reports, reaffirming the company's commitment to its manufacturing operations in the world's largest auto market.

Musk made the remarks on Thursday during a meeting with Ren Hongbin, chairman of the China Council for the Promotion of International Trade, in Shenzhen, according to Yuyuan Tantian, a social media account affiliated with Chinese state broadcaster CCTV.

Tesla's (TSLA) Shanghai factory delivered over 810K Model 3 and Model Y vehicles in the first 10 months of 2026, up 21.4% from the same period last year. The facility currently has an annual vehicle production capacity of more than 950K units and serves as a key manufacturing and export hub for the automaker, shipping vehicles to markets including Europe, South Korea and Australia.

During the meeting, Musk described himself as a "superfan" of China, praising the country's architecture, natural landscapes, and railway system. He was quoted as saying, "China is cool. I have always encouraged people from all over the world to come to China and see these amazing places with their own eyes. There are incredible cities, incredible natural scenery, and world wonders like the Terracotta Army."

"The more the US and China cooperate, the better off both will be," Musk added, according to Xinhua News Agency, as reported by Chinese media.

Musk arrived in Shenzhen on November 18 with a US delegation to attend events associated with the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week. Chinese media described the visit as his first publicly reported trip to the city. Upon arriving, Musk posted on X: "Is the Thucydides Trap ever avoidable? I wish it were, but, inevitably, the most interesting outcome is the most likely."

The Thucydides Trap refers to the risk of conflict that can arise when an emerging power challenges an established one, as intensifying competition between the two raises geopolitical tensions.

A video released also showed Musk interacting with his young son, who accompanied him to the meeting. Musk asked his son, "Did you love China?" to which the boy replied, "Yes." Musk then joked that his son's toys were all labelled "Made in China," adding that this made him look forward to visiting the country.

data.title: AbbVie inks up to $2.54B bispecific cancer drug deal with DISCO Pharma
data.description:
AbbVie (ABBV) has agreed to pay up to $2.54B to collaborate with Germany-based biotech DISCO Pharmaceuticals on the development of novel cancer treatments, marking an early-stage expansion of the drugmaker's efforts in next-generation bispecific therapies.

Bispecific antibodies, which are designed to simultaneously target two different proteins, are attracting growing interest from major pharmaceutical companies, including Bristol Myers Squibb (BMY), Pfizer (PFE) and Merck (MRK), as the industry explores new approaches to treating cancer.

Disco will receive $40M upfront and up to $2.5B in milestone payments ⁠as part of the deal to develop so-called AND-gated bispecific therapeutics for ​solid tumors. It will also be eligible for tiered royalties on worldwide net sales. The ​approach is designed to recognize cancer cells only when two target proteins are present simultaneously, potentially reducing damage to healthy tissue, the companies said.

“The collaboration with AbbVie represents an important opportunity to deliver the next generation of precision medicines to patients with difficult-to-treat solid tumors,” said Mark Manfredi, CEO of DISCO Pharmaceuticals. “Our AND-gated approach is designed to selectively target tumor cells while sparing healthy tissue, thus offering a potentially differentiated path in precision oncology."

Manfredi's company ​will be responsible for the research and discovery. AbbVie will have the ​right to exclusively license selected programs for further development.

data.title: Michael Burry questions progress on Wall Street’s massive Nvidia financing initiative
data.description:
Big short investor Michael Burry highlighted a lack of progress in a $500B financing initiative involving Nvidia (NVDA) and some of Wall Street’s biggest financial institutions, noting that no capital has been deployed despite earlier commitments.

In a post on X on Thursday, Burry shared a report by The Wall Street Journal stating that several financial firms had pledged in August to mobilize funds to help Nvidia (NVDA) customers finance purchases of AI chips. However, the funding is yet to materialize.

The initiative involves Apollo Global Management (APO), Blackstone (BX), BlackRock (BLK), Brookfield Asset Management (BAM), Goldman Sachs (GS) and KKR (KKR).

The initiative was driven by Nvidia (NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang's efforts to expand financing options for customers amid growing demand for AI computing capacity. However, the commitments were made through a nonbinding memorandum of understanding, meaning the firms were not obligated to raise a specific amount.

The discussions have faced hurdles over Nvidia's (NVDA) proposed credit guarantees of up to 25% of project costs, with lenders seeking stronger protections. Talks on the first chip-backed financing deal are ongoing, but no agreement is expected before next year, the report added.

data.title: SELLAS Life Sciences prices $150M public offering of common stock
data.description:
• SELLAS Life Sciences Group (SLS) priced an underwritten public offering of 11.54M shares of common stock at $13 per share, generating expected gross proceeds of $150M before underwriting discounts, commissions and offering expenses.
  • The underwriters a 30-day option to purchase up to an additional 1.73M shares at the offering price, less applicable discounts and commissions.
